definition: Run the practice across the structural gap between doing the work and being paid for it. The instrument is a three-state pipeline view - booked but not yet travelled, travelled but not yet paid, and received - refreshed at each close so the advisor can see how much of the next months' cash is already determined and how much still has to be sold. Because the calendar that matters is travel dates rather than booking dates, seasonality lands differently than it feels: the quiet selling months may pay well and the busiest selling weeks may pay nothing for two seasons. On top of that sits a reserve sized in qualitative terms against the practice's own reversal exposure and its thinnest historical stretch, and a draw discipline that pays the advisor from received-and-non-reversible revenue rather than from statements that are still provisional. The levers available are real but limited: fee capture timing pulls some revenue forward, product and lead-time mix changes the shape of the curve, and declining chronically underwater work frees the hours that produce revenue at all. Sizing is judgement against the practice's own history; no benchmark figure applies.

included: the booked, travelled and received pipeline view
reserve sizing against reversal exposure and thin stretches as a qualitative judgement
the levers that reshape the cash curve
excluded: borrowing, credit or investment decisions and any personalized financial advice
bookkeeping and tax
pricing or fee-level design - agency-models KB

pros.claim: A three-state pipeline shows how much of the coming quarter is already sold and how much is still hope
pros.example: an advisor seeing that most of next quarter's cash sits in trips already travelling and choosing to invest that time in acquisition

pros.claim: Paying the advisor only from non-reversible received revenue prevents a personal cash crisis caused by a business reversal
pros.example: a cancelled group producing an offset that lands harmlessly because it was never drawn against

cons.claim: Holding a reserve in a practice with thin margins can feel like starving the business of the marketing it needs
cons.example: a reserve held through a slow winter while a promising destination campaign is postponed

cons.claim: The pipeline view is only as honest as the expectation rows behind it, so its confidence is borrowed
cons.example: a healthy-looking quarter resting on rows whose commissionable base was never verified

failure_modes: drawing personal income from provisional commission
planning the year on booking seasonality instead of travel seasonality
carrying no reserve in a business whose revenue can be recalled
cutting the reserve to fund work that the margin review already showed is underwater
acceptance_tests: the pipeline separates booked, travelled-not-paid and received, and the practice's spendable figure counts only the last of the three net of provisional lines
a stated reserve intention exists and is expressed against the practice's own reversal exposure and thin-season history
revisit_triggers: a season lands materially away from the pipeline's expectation
reversal exposure rises after a run of cancellations
the product mix or typical lead time shifts

base.update_signal: actual receipts diverge materially from the pipeline forecast for a period, or reversal exposure changes shape

definition: Execute the fee decision the practice has already made, which is a different skill from designing it. Capture means the fee is agreed and collected before design work starts, under written engagement terms that state plainly what the fee buys - discovery, research, itinerary design, a defined number of revisions, booking and document management, in-trip support - and what it does not buy, that it is payment for advisory work rather than a markup on the trip, and whether it is credited against a booking, non-refundable, or partly both. It travels on a payment rail the practice controls with a receipt issued, and it is recorded as its own revenue line, because unlike commission it is earned when the work is done rather than when someone travels. The hard part is the awkward cases: a client asking for the fee to be waived, a client who pays the fee and then books directly, a client who cancels mid-design, and a referred prospect who did not know a fee existed. Each is answered from the terms the client already signed rather than improvised in the moment.

included: pre-work collection sequence and written scope of the engagement
refund, credit and cancellation policy as issued to the client
handling waiver, direct-booking and mid-design cancellation requests
excluded: whether to charge a fee and at what level, and the client-alignment argument for fee models - agency-models KB
quoting or discounting trip prices
any statement of a market-typical fee amount

pros.claim: A fee collected before design work makes the advisor's time the thing being paid for, which is what it actually is
pros.example: a multi-week itinerary build that starts only after the engagement is signed and the fee has cleared

pros.claim: Written scope converts the most common client conflicts into a reference rather than a negotiation
pros.example: a fifth round of revisions answered by the revision clause the client accepted at the start

cons.claim: Asking for money before producing anything loses some prospects, especially referrals expecting free advice
cons.example: a referred enquirer who assumed the service was free because the referrer never mentioned the fee

cons.claim: A fee sets a service expectation the practice must then honour under time pressure
cons.example: a fee-paying client expecting same-day responses during a week the advisor is managing a disruption for someone else

failure_modes: starting design work on a verbal promise of payment
issuing terms that never state the refund or credit position
waiving the fee case by case until it means nothing
positioning the fee as a discount on the trip rather than payment for advice
acceptance_tests: no design work begins before signed engagement terms and a cleared fee, or a recorded, deliberate exception
the issued terms state what the fee buys, what it excludes and the refund or credit position, and the client has a receipt
revisit_triggers: clients repeatedly push back at the same point in the terms
a mid-design cancellation exposes an unclear clause
the practice changes what is included in the service

base.update_signal: clients consistently object at one clause, or a cancellation or direct-booking case exposes terms that do not answer it

definition: Compare, per engagement and then per class of engagement, the hours actually consumed against the revenue that actually arrived. Hours include the invisible ones: discovery calls, research on a destination never booked, itinerary revisions, supplier chasing, document assembly, in-trip messages across time zones, and the post-trip follow-up. Revenue means received and non-reversible commission after the split, plus fees collected, plus add-on commission - not booking value and not expected commission. The output is deliberately a qualitative ranking rather than a computed margin: which trip types, supplier categories and client patterns reliably pay for the time they take, which are break-even but strategically worth keeping because they feed referrals, and which are chronically underwater. That ranking is what makes the practice's hardest decisions decidable - who to invite back through the cadence, which enquiries to decline or redirect, where a fee has to carry work that commission never will. No industry benchmark is imported; the comparison is against the practice's own history and the advisor's own capacity.

included: capturing true hours including unbilled and post-trip time
measuring against received non-reversible revenue
the qualitative ranking of engagement classes and the decline decision it supports
excluded: setting fee levels or rate cards - agency-models KB
any benchmark margin or industry-average figure
judging suppliers on service quality rather than economics - trip-design KB

pros.claim: Counting the invisible hours exposes work that felt profitable and never was
pros.example: a complex multi-country itinerary with many revisions that realized less than a repeat cruise booking taking a fraction of the time

pros.claim: A ranking makes declining work a business decision rather than a personal rejection
pros.example: an enquiry type the practice can honestly redirect because the record shows it never pays for its hours

cons.claim: Time tracking is tedious and the first thing to lapse, which biases the sample toward remembered painful cases
cons.example: only the frustrating engagements getting logged, making the average look worse than it is

cons.claim: Pure economics undervalues engagements whose real return is the referrals they generate
cons.example: a low-value honeymoon booking whose family produces several later trips

failure_modes: measuring against booking value instead of received revenue
excluding post-trip and support time from the hours
declining a class of work on one bad case
importing an outside benchmark instead of comparing with the practice's own record
acceptance_tests: each reviewed engagement shows hours including support and post-trip time against received, non-reversible revenue
engagement classes are ranked into pays-for-itself, strategic break-even and chronically underwater with the evidence attached
revisit_triggers: the practice adds a new trip type or client segment
a class ranked underwater changes after a fee or scope change
capacity changes because of hours available or staffing

base.update_signal: a full cycle of tracked engagements changes the ranking of a trip type, or capacity assumptions change

definition: Before a single protection plan is presented, establish which obligation classes apply to this advisor in this jurisdiction and under this affiliation. The classes to identify and verify are: whether selling or soliciting travel insurance requires a producer or limited-lines licence class, whether the advisor must be appointed by the insurer or may operate under the host's or a program's licence, how seller-of-travel registration classes interact with offering insurance, what the applicable rules define as merely describing a product versus soliciting, recommending or advising on it, what must be disclosed about the advisor's compensation, and what records must be kept and for how long. The verification act is the point of the unit: confirm current requirements with the relevant regulator and with the host and insurer rather than with a peer, a social-media thread or a memory of last year, and re-verify at renewal and on any change of state, residence or affiliation. Requirements differ by state, province and country and change; nothing here states what any jurisdiction currently requires. If the class cannot be confirmed, the practice books the travel and refers the client to a licensed source instead of offering.

included: naming the licensing, appointment, disclosure and record-keeping classes that may apply
the verification act with regulator, insurer and host, and its cadence
the fallback of booking travel only and referring the client to a licensed source
excluded: stating what any jurisdiction requires, what a licence is called, or what any threshold or exemption is
the registration and entity decisions of the practice - agency-models KB
legal advice of any kind

pros.claim: Verifying the class before offering keeps a revenue line from being built on ground that has to be abandoned
pros.example: an add-on script and client expectation created before discovering that the offer route required an appointment the advisor did not hold

pros.claim: Knowing where describing ends and advising begins gives the advisor a usable sentence under pressure
pros.example: a client pressing for a coverage opinion and receiving a clear referral to the insurer instead of an improvised answer

cons.claim: Verification is slow, involves several bodies, and must be repeated rather than done once
cons.example: a practice that adds clients in another state having to re-check before offering there

cons.claim: The conservative line can cost real revenue and leave clients less protected in the meantime
cons.example: declining to present any plan while a class is unconfirmed, and a client travelling with no protection at all

failure_modes: taking a peer's or a forum's word for what is required
assuming the host's licence covers the advisor without confirming the arrangement in writing
verifying once at start-up and never at renewal or after moving
offering while the class is unresolved because the sale is in front of you
acceptance_tests: the applicable obligation classes are written down with the body that confirmed each and the date of confirmation
no protection product is presented to a client before that record exists, and the fallback referral path is documented
revisit_triggers: a licence, appointment or registration renewal falls due
the practice, the advisor's residence or the client base moves into another jurisdiction
the host or insurer changes the arrangement under which offers are made

base.update_signal: a regulator, insurer or host restates the requirements, or the practice's jurisdictional footprint changes

definition: Make the protection offer a fixed part of the booking process rather than a judgement call about who looks like a buyer, and record what happened. The offer sits at a defined point in the sequence - typically at or before deposit, because several benefit classes in these products carry purchase-timing conditions relative to the initial trip payment, and again at final payment where the plan permits - and it goes to every client, including the ones an advisor assumes will decline. What is recorded is dated and specific: that protection was offered, which product family was described, what materials were provided, and what the client decided, in the client's own words where possible. The record protects the client, who never gets quietly skipped because of an assumption about their budget, and it protects the advisor when a disruption later prompts the question of what was said. Declines are accepted at face value and logged; the answer 'my credit card covers it' is noted as the client's own statement and referred back to the card issuer, never assessed by the advisor.

included: a fixed offer point tied to purchase-timing mechanics
universal offering regardless of assumed buying intent
the dated offer-and-decision record and how declines are logged
excluded: assessing another product's coverage such as a credit-card benefit
recommending a specific plan to a specific traveller
re-raising the offer as a pressure tactic - the ethical rule governs that

pros.claim: A fixed offer point means nobody is skipped because the advisor guessed at their budget
pros.example: a modest-budget client who buys protection precisely because the trip's nonrefundable deposit matters more to them

pros.claim: A dated decision record answers the hardest post-disruption question in one line
pros.example: a client insisting they were never told, met with the note recording the offer, the materials sent and their decline

cons.claim: Offering to everyone in a fixed way can feel scripted to clients who have already declined before
cons.example: a repeat client asked again at the same point on their third trip and reading it as a sales routine

cons.claim: Timing the offer to purchase-window mechanics adds pressure to an early conversation
cons.example: raising protection at deposit while the client is still deciding whether to travel at all

failure_modes: deciding in advance who will not buy
offering verbally and recording nothing
letting the offer slide past the point where timing-sensitive benefit classes are still available
interpreting a client's existing credit-card or employer coverage on their behalf
acceptance_tests: every booking file shows a dated offer-and-decision record naming the product family described and the client's decision
no file shows a booking where protection was never offered without a recorded reason
revisit_triggers: the plan's purchase-timing conditions or the offer route change
a disruption exposes a file with no offer record
the requirement class for the jurisdiction changes

base.update_signal: a file surfaces without an offer record, or the product's purchase-timing conditions or offer route change

definition: Hold the conversation that makes the offer honest: map the exposure this particular trip actually creates, then point the client at the documents that decide it. The exposure map is concrete and specific to the itinerary - how much money is nonrefundable and when the penalty ladder steps up, how remote the destinations are and what medical or evacuation exposure that implies, how many connections the trip depends on, whether travelling companions' circumstances are linked, whether anyone's health history brings the look-back and purchase-timing mechanics into play, and whether the client's real worry is a named-peril cancellation or the broader cancel-for-any-reason class. What the advisor supplies is the trip's risk picture and the product's own documents; what the advisor does not supply is an interpretation of the wording, an opinion on whether a specific condition or circumstance would be covered, or any prediction of a claim outcome. The client is directed to the plan documents and the insurer or a licensed producer for those, and the referral is noted. The test of the conversation is that a client who declines still understands exactly what they are carrying themselves.

included: mapping the trip's own exposure in concrete terms
naming benefit categories and timing mechanics generically and pointing to the plan documents
recording the referral to insurer or licensed producer for interpretation
excluded: interpreting policy wording or exclusions
assessing a specific traveller's medical history or circumstances
predicting or promising a claim outcome

pros.claim: An exposure map lets the client make the decision on facts about their own trip rather than on fear or bravado
pros.example: a client seeing that most of their trip cost becomes nonrefundable on a date months before departure and deciding accordingly

pros.claim: The describe-and-refer line is protective for both sides and can be said out loud without awkwardness
pros.example: handing over the plan documents and the insurer's contact for a coverage question instead of guessing at an answer

cons.claim: Clients often want a yes-or-no answer and experience a referral as evasion
cons.example: a client asking whether a parent's condition is covered and hearing what sounds like a dodge

cons.claim: Mapping exposure well takes time on a conversation that may end in a decline
cons.example: a long fit conversation on a complex multigenerational trip where nobody buys

failure_modes: summarizing coverage in the advisor's own words and creating an expectation the plan does not carry
opining on a medical situation or a pre-existing condition
presenting the broader cancel-for-any-reason class as though it covered everything
leaving the client unable to state what they are exposed to if they decline
acceptance_tests: the file records the trip-specific exposures discussed and the documents or contacts handed to the client
no advisor-authored summary of coverage or exclusions appears in place of the plan's own documents
revisit_triggers: the trip changes materially in cost, itinerary or party composition
the product's benefit categories or timing mechanics change
a client complaint or claim shows the conversation was misunderstood

base.update_signal: a claim, complaint or regulator guidance shows the describe-and-refer line was crossed or misunderstood

definition: Bind the whole recommending surface of the practice with rules that outrank the sale. Present risk factually and proportionately, using the trip's own numbers and dates rather than catastrophe stories, because fear-selling produces purchases clients resent and reputations that do not survive a claim. Disclose compensation at the moment of recommending, not buried afterwards: that the advisor is paid when a protection plan is bought, that supplier and preferred-program relationships exist where they do, and that these relationships never decide which option is put forward first. Take deliberate extra care where a client is vulnerable - bereaved, recently diagnosed, elderly and tired, cognitively loaded, buying under pressure from a relative, or working in a second language: slow the pace, put the material in writing, invite a support person if the client wants one, and confirm understanding rather than agreement. Accept a decline the first time it is given, record it, and re-raise only if a genuinely material trip fact changes. Never trade a benefit for a review, an endorsement or a referral, and never let a compensation difference steer a recommendation without saying so.

included: compensation disclosure at the point of recommendation
the no-fear-selling standard and proportionate risk framing
vulnerable-client care and the accept-the-decline rule
the ban on traded endorsements and undisclosed steering
excluded: the compliance obligations themselves, which are named as classes in the requirement unit
product comparison and coverage interpretation
clinical or capacity assessment of any client

pros.claim: Disclosure survives contact with a bad outcome in a way that persuasion does not
pros.example: a client whose claim is denied still trusting the advisor because they were told at the outset who pays the advisor and who decides claims

pros.claim: Accepting a decline once protects the relationship that produces the next several bookings
pros.example: a client who declined protection twice still referring two households because they never felt pushed

cons.claim: Honest, unpressured selling converts fewer add-ons than fear-based selling in the short run
cons.example: a lower attachment rate than a competitor who opens with a hospital-bill anecdote

cons.claim: Compensation disclosure invites a price conversation the advisor may not want
cons.example: a client asking why they should not book direct once they learn a supplier pays the advisor

failure_modes: using catastrophe stories to close
disclosing compensation only in fine print or after the decision
re-raising a declined offer until the client relents
pressing a bereaved or overwhelmed client because the window is closing
offering an incentive in exchange for a public review or an endorsement
acceptance_tests: every recommendation that carries advisor compensation shows a contemporaneous disclosure in the client's channel of record
declines are recorded once and not re-raised in the file without a documented material change in the trip
revisit_triggers: a complaint alleges pressure, surprise about compensation or unclear framing
the practice adds an incentive, referral reward or preferred-program arrangement
a vulnerable-client situation is handled and reviewed

base.update_signal: a complaint, review or claim outcome shows a client felt pressured or uninformed about how the advisor is paid
